request.title: What a Cat's Slow Blink Really Means
request.provider_topic: Do cats understand a human slow blink?
request.narration: Your cat's slow blink might be a reply. In one experiment, owners slow-blinked at their cats. Cats half-blinked and narrowed their eyes more than when owners sat nearby without interacting. In a second experiment, an unfamiliar researcher slow-blinked at cats. The cats were then more likely to approach her hand than after a neutral face. A slow blink is not one long stare. It is a series of half-blinks, then a prolonged narrowing or full closure of the eyes. The authors suggest this may be positive communication. They also caution that more research is needed before firm conclusions about the cat's emotional state. So try one slow blink from a comfortable distance, then watch. If the cat looks away or stays tense, give it space. The blink is an invitation, not a demand.
